analysis:
Both units are BASE-side text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md, lines 1624-2515. The changed base ranges in file_changes are 1256-1410, so neither unit contains a changed line. I found no new behavior here, only unchanged documentation. I examined the uninstall, restart, status, doctor, models, benchmark, update, beta, fan, login/logout, enroll/unenroll and logs sections against the threat model.

The uninstall text says it refuses symlinks, mount points and anything resolving outside Darkbloom's folders. It also says it never deletes Keychain items or a chosen models folder, and revokes the account token on a best-effort basis (A-008). This matches the retained descriptions of TB-003, TB-011 and the cache threat T-041. The prefix-cache documentation in this range, `~/Library/Caches/darkbloom` and the SSD prefix-cache status, is consistent with T-041's HMAC-named, encrypted, TTL-bounded design. I saw no claim in these lines that weakens the 30-minute TTL, the KEK-based purge or the account-scoped salt. The App Attest text keeps serving authorization tied to an unexpired lease and a fresh coordinator decision, consistent with T-053 and T-057. No secrets, endpoint changes or new trust claims appear.

The patch excerpt is truncated. It shows a new `darkbloom sandbox setup --disk <volume>` option at head lines 1270 and 1286-1301. That option affects the TB-013 installer and add-on boundary (T-061) and the operator-selected volume handling. It is outside the supplied units, so I cannot assess the path validation or the pass-through to the installer. Reviewers of the units covering head lines 1256-1450 should check that the `--disk` path validation and argument passing do not enable injection and do not weaken the T-061 trust assumptions. I am not raising a finding from this unit set.
